solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Asian boss almost sacked merchant's friend

indicators.note: sacked suggests the letters are ransacked and thrown about, so they are rearranged
almost means the word boss stops short of its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: An Asian manager has nearly fired someone's merchant friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts BOSS to BOS; 'sacked' then rearranges ASIAN plus BOS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice, Antonio is the merchant and this character is his close friend.

clue.text: Being so could make a fellow blush furiously?

definitions.text: Being so could make a fellow blush furiously?

indicators.note: furiously suggests wild agitation, so the letters are churned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Shyness might make a man go red in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furiously' rearranges A, F and BLUSH; the whole clue also describes shyness making someone colour up.
explanation.definitionFit: Shy people are prone to blushing, so the clue's whole description fits timidity.

clue.text: First off, not the right chap to support weight? On the contrary

definitions.text: First off, not the right chap to support weight? On the contrary

indicators.note: in a down answer, the lower piece supports the one above it, so this piece goes beneath

parts.note: ST is short for stone, a British unit of weight

indicators.note: first off means the opening letter of the phrase is removed

parts.note: something wrong is not the right one
a man is a chap

explanation.surface: A puzzle about whether some fellow is suited to lifting heavy weights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips the surface's doubt: the answer is precisely the right chap to bear heavy weight, so the clue works as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus or competition performer famed for lifting heavy loads is the very person to support weight.

clue.text: Record-keeper dictated for Freud, perhaps

indicators.note: dictated means spoken aloud for someone to write down, so we want a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a chronicler who keeps yearly records is an annalist

explanation.surface: A secretary taking dictation from Sigmund Freud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dictated' signals that the word for a writer of annals is heard, giving a word spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud founded psychoanalysis, so he is an example of a psychoanalyst, often shortened to this word.

clue.text: Head to toe, William's bloody rude

indicators.note: head to toe means the first letter of the name goes to its foot, here just after the rest of the name

parts.note: Bill is the familiar short form of William
something bloody is red

explanation.surface: Someone called William is crude from top to bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head to toe' sounds like a whole-body description, but it shifts the first letter of the short name to its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone badly brought up lacks manners, so rude and this hyphenated adjective are synonyms.

clue.text: Rather small-minded about regulations, for a start

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: petty means small-minded and mean-spirited

indicators.note: for a start means only the opening letter of regulations is used

explanation.surface: Someone is somewhat narrow-minded about rules, to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rather' at the front looks like an adverb modifying the clue, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb this word means fairly or quite, as in 'pretty good', so it matches rather.

clue.text: Force into action super-injunction, perhaps to conceal name

indicators.note: to conceal means the first piece hides the second inside it

parts.note: a super-injunction is an example of a court order gagging the newspapers, a press gag

explanation.surface: A celebrity uses a super-injunction to keep their name out of the papers.
explanation.walkthrough: A super-injunction is a British court order banning the press from reporting even that the order exists.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically gangs seized men into naval service; as a verb it now means to coerce someone into doing something.

clue.text: Restrain one leaving and heading for tradesman's entrance

indicators.note: leaving means the letter for one departs from the word

parts.note: to enchain is to bind in chains, to restrain
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: heading for means just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Restraining someone who tries to slip out through the tradesman's entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' is the verb (en-TRANCE), not a doorway; the tradesman's entrance is a side door for deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance is to captivate or put under a spell, which is to bewitch or charm.

clue.text: One that's dragged along for film preview

definitions.meaning: a wagon or caravan towed behind a vehicle
a short advert showing clips of a forthcoming movie

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a towed vehicle and a cinema promotional clip, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Second route for public transport will conserve energy and improve efficiency

indicators.note: will conserve means the line keeps the next piece safe inside it

parts.note: a tramline is the track a tram runs along
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A second tram route would save energy and make the network run better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conserve energy' reads as green policy, but it puts E inside TRAMLINE.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a process simpler and more economical is to rationalise it, which raises its efficiency.

clue.text: A greeting from Brescia originally?

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An Italian hello said to come first from the city of Brescia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' looks like the first-letter signal, but the run spans the end of Brescia and the start of originally.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the informal Italian word used for hello or goodbye, so it is a greeting.

clue.text: You can't be yourself at this social event

definitions.text: You can't be yourself at this social event

parts.words: You can't be yourself at this social event
parts.note: guests come in costume as somebody else, so nobody is themselves

explanation.definitionFit: At a costume party guests dress as other characters, so they literally cannot appear as themselves.

clue.text: Narrow hat worn by European bloke backwards

indicators.note: a hat worn by someone sits around their head, so the hat goes round the next piece

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat

indicators.note: backwards means the European and the bloke are read in reverse

parts.note: Tim is a man's name, any bloke

explanation.surface: A European man wears a narrow-brimmed hat back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backwards' turns E and the bloke round to make MITE; 'worn by' places the hat around that.
explanation.definitionFit: Something restricted in scope is narrow, as with a small or confined range.

clue.text: Former First Lady must accept snub by current administration

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: must accept means the lady takes the following pieces inside her

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis

indicators.note: by means beside, so the current follows the snub

parts.note: to cut someone is to snub them
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An ex-First Lady must put up with being snubbed by the present government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' suggests a president's wife, but it is Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: The branch of government that runs affairs, or the management of an organisation, is its administration.

clue.text: Chicken Madras, with starter halved, ordered — that'll take time

indicators.note: that'll take means the rearranged letters take the next piece inside
ordered means the letters are put into a new order
the starter is the opening letter, a Roman thousand; halving it gives the Roman five hundred

explanation.surface: Ordering a chicken madras and half a starter in a curry house that will be slow to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: M (1000) halved is D (500), making DADRAS; 'ordered' rearranges it to DASARD and T goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A coward is called chicken, and this old word means a contemptible coward.

clue.text: Tony gets worried after a crowd arises, showing hate

indicators.note: after means these pieces follow the A and crowd
arises means the word goes upwards, read from bottom to top in a down answer

parts.note: a mob is a crowd
tony means fashionable or stylish, which is in
ate in the sense of 'what ate him?', troubled or worried

explanation.surface: Tony is upset when a mob rises up and shows hatred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tony' looks like a name but is the adjective meaning stylish, giving IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe or detest something intensely is a stronger synonym of to hate it.

clue.text: Farmer gets more sexy — sounds like you and I missed out

indicators.note: missed out means those letters are removed from the longer word

parts.note: raunchier means more sexually explicit

indicators.note: sounds like says the next word is represented by the letter pronounced the same

parts.note: the letter U is pronounced like the word you

explanation.surface: A farmer is getting sexier, though 'you and I' are left out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds like' turns 'you' into U; both U and I come out of RAUNCHIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who runs a large livestock farm, especially in America, is a kind of farmer.

clue.text: High achiever wants one poor grade struck off record

indicators.note: high means intoxicated, so the letters are tipsy and jumbled
struck off means that letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: E is a low mark in a school grading scale

explanation.surface: A top student must have one bad mark removed from the school record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High achiever' reads as one phrase, but High is the anagram signal; ACHIEVER less one E is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A collection of historical documents kept for reference is a record of the past.

clue.text: Close agreement

definitions.meaning: an adjective meaning dense, tightly packed together
a formal pact or treaty between parties

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means closely packed; as a noun it means a treaty or pact.

clue.text: For example, before special summons to meal, knocked back drinks

indicators.note: before means this piece comes ahead of the rest

parts.note: eg is short for exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: knocked back means the next pieces are turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a gong is struck to call people to dinner

explanation.surface: Someone downs drinks before a special dinner gong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking, but it reverses S and GONG to GNOGS.
explanation.definitionFit: A creamy mixture of eggs, milk and spirits served at Christmas is a type of drink.

clue.text: Opening in shell-like structure's bottom has a function — absorbing gas

indicators.note: bottom means the last letter, the foot of the word in a down entry
absorbing means the function takes the gas inside it

parts.note: a role is a function or job
H is the symbol for hydrogen, a gas

explanation.surface: Describes a shell-shaped structure whose base performs a function by absorbing gas.
explanation.walkthrough: Shell-like is British slang for an ear, as in 'a word in your shell-like'.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening of the ear, informally, is the hole leading into it, an aural opening.

clue.text: Most serious parties will be invested with the trappings of government

indicators.note: invested with means clothed in, so the parties go inside the outer letters
trappings are the outer adornments, so just the outer letters of the word are used

parts.note: raves are wild parties

explanation.surface: The most serious political parties will take on the trappings of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trappings of government' are G and T, which go round RAVES.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the superlative of grave, meaning most solemn or serious.

clue.text: Attractive, but somewhat left out

indicators.note: out means the letter for left is removed from the word

parts.note: slightly means to a small degree, somewhat

explanation.surface: Pleasant to look at, though a little excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' reads as a phrase, but 'left' gives L and 'out' removes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The rarer opposite of unsightly, it means pleasing to the eye, good-looking.

clue.text: It leads to dudes getting romance, put another way?

definitions.text: It leads to dudes getting romance, put another way?

indicators.note: another way means the letters are set out in a different arrangement
leads means the first letters of the preceding words, the ones at the front

explanation.surface: A way of finding love that helps guys get together with partners.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials of It, to, dudes, getting (ITDG) join ROMANCE and PUT, and 'another way' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Matching couples by machine leads people to romance, so the whole clue describes this service.

clue.text: Magpie's size related to type

definitions.meaning: the scientific genus name of the magpie
a printing measure, a typeface size of twelve points

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the Latin genus of the magpie and an old printer's unit of type size.

clue.text: Keen on angry speech about extremely little, being this?

definitions.text: Keen on angry speech about extremely little, being this?

parts.note: into means keen on, as in 'really into jazz'

indicators.note: extremely means the extreme letters, first and last, of the word

parts.note: a rant is an angry tirade

explanation.surface: Someone ranting furiously over trifles must be narrow-minded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely little' gives LE, the outer letters; the clue as a whole describes the bigot it builds.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who loves fuming about trivia lacks tolerance, so the description fits a bigoted person.

clue.text: Busy person having to hurry, missing bus, gets car

parts.note: a busy bee is a hard-working person

indicators.note: missing means the word bus is taken out of the hurry word

parts.note: to bustle is to hurry about

explanation.surface: A busy commuter who misses the bus has to rush and get a car instead.
explanation.walkthrough: The Volkswagen of this name is a classic small car.
explanation.definitionFit: The Volkswagen model nicknamed for its insect-like shape is a well-known car.

clue.text: Tough guy loses heart after shocking tale

indicators.note: after means the guy follows the rearranged tale
shocking means scandalous or appalling, so the letters are disturbed into a new order
loses heart means the middle letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: Henry is a man's name, standing for any guy

explanation.surface: A tough man gets discouraged after hearing a shocking story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses heart' sounds like despair, but it removes the central N from HENRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat that is hard and chewy like hide is tough, so the two words are synonyms.
